content.title: Crystal-Heart Offering | Object Approach, Brief Occlusion and Paired Gift
content.summary: An adult jeweler offers two crystal leaves through a bounded lens-near interaction. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing all source-specific surfaces.

quick_start.input_format: Two clearly adult diners and two bowls persist. + Only one synchronized bite initiates the test. + Reactions escalate after ingestion. + The shared look precedes relief. + Two matching relief objects complete the terminal state.
quick_start.recommended_input: One original adult jeweler holds one teal crystal leaf at chest height and looks into camera. Return the same leaf to chest height, revealing the unchanged face and silver costume. Hold both leaves symmetrically beside the face and finish with one small smile and steady eye contact.
required_anchors: One clearly adult identity and fixed environment persist.
The first object remains the same through approach and retreat.
The second object is added rather than substituted.
The final state clearly shows both gifts.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.

creative_dna.mechanism: 同一成年角色在固定粉紫棚景依次举起两颗虹彩水晶心，让物件从胸前靠近镜头并产生短暂遮挡，再分别回到双手；人物始终直视镜头，终局以双心并列和微笑确认赠礼。 The reusable mechanism preserves causal order, spatial anchors and the final proof while replacing every source-specific person, location, object, wording, choreography and design.

invariants.rule: One clearly adult identity and fixed environment persist.
invariants.purpose: Establishes the baseline identity, object or geography that every later state must preserve.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact baseline rule, later changes cannot be attributed to the same subject, object or place, so the sequence loses its reference state. Removed rule: "One clearly adult identity and fixed environment persist."

invariants.rule: The first object remains the same through approach and retreat.
invariants.purpose: Makes the visible trigger precede and explain the first mechanism response.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact trigger rule, the response appears spontaneously and the central cause-and-effect claim is no longer demonstrated. Removed rule: "The first object remains the same through approach and retreat."

invariants.rule: Lens occlusion is brief and bounded.
invariants.purpose: Keeps the middle progression registered instead of allowing an unexplained reset.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact progression rule, the middle can jump to a replacement state and the accumulated result is no longer traceable. Removed rule: "Lens occlusion is brief and bounded."

invariants.rule: The second object is added rather than substituted.
invariants.purpose: Reconnects the changed or partial state to the established subject and spatial anchor.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact reconnection rule, detail or transformed shots can belong to a different subject or geography and continuity cannot be verified. Removed rule: "The second object is added rather than substituted."

invariants.rule: The final state clearly shows both gifts.
invariants.purpose: Turns the terminal hold into observable proof that the mechanism completed.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact terminal-proof rule, the sequence stops on motion alone and never confirms the promised outcome or preserved aftermath. Removed rule: "The final state clearly shows both gifts."
